entries.exactPassage: Here’s the tension: the dimensions are connected. Financial legacy without values legacy creates entitled heirs. Values legacy without financial legacy limits what you can do. Social impact without environmental awareness is short-sighted. The four dimensions are not separate. They are one structure. The architect who only builds one wall builds nothing that stands. The architect who builds all four builds something that outlasts her — and serves everyone who enters.

entries.proposedWording: Describe a possible risk or question to consider, not an inevitable family outcome. Retain the architecture metaphor and invitation to connect dimensions.

entries.exactPassage: Wills — The Basics: "A will is a legal document that says what happens to your belongings after you die. In South Africa, for a will to be valid, it must be: in writing, signed by you, and signed by two witnesses — who cannot be beneficiaries. If you leave something to a witness, that gift is void. The law is precise. Follow the rules."
entries.concern: The short checklist omits signing/presence/page/special requirements; beneficiary-witness consequences have exceptions and differ from automatically invalidating the entire will.
entries.proposedWording: Use qualified current South African guidance: age/capacity and competent witnesses matter; signing at the end, presence and relevant pages/special forms matter. A beneficiary witness generally risks disqualification, with statutory exceptions requiring advice.
entries.implementationImpact: Separate reviewed learner-source proposal; no source correction in this teacher-guide batch. Preserve stable lesson/block/prompt/response identities through explicit compiler mapping before any source release. Legal proposals require qualified South African review.

entries.exactPassage: "You do not need a lawyer to make a will. But you do need to follow the requirements exactly. A handwritten will on a piece of paper, signed by you and two witnesses who are not beneficiaries, is legally valid. A fancy typed document missing one signature is not."
entries.concern: Handwriting plus a count of signatures is not a complete validity test, and defects can have different consequences.
entries.proposedWording: A handwritten document may be a will if all applicable requirements are satisfied. A simplified classroom checklist cannot certify validity; obtain qualified help, including where a defect may require court consideration.

entries.exactPassage: Trusts — The Deeper Layer: "A trust is like a container. You put assets into it. You set rules for how and when those assets are distributed. A trustee manages the trust according to your instructions. Trusts are useful when: you have minor children, you want to control how money is used, you want to protect assets from creditors, or you want to avoid family disputes."
entries.concern: A trust is not an automatic creditor shield or guarantee against disputes; trustees have legal duties beyond carrying out personal instructions.
entries.proposedWording: A trust can serve specified purposes subject to law, proper administration, cost, tax and duties. Suitability and protection depend on facts and qualified advice.

entries.exactPassage: Key idea: Adv. Mkhize's warning is stark: if the form is wrong, your intentions mean nothing. The paradox: a will is both powerful and fragile. entries.proposedWording: Explain that defects and disqualification issues differ and may involve statutory exceptions or court consideration. Do not determine real validity from the classroom examples.

entries.exactPassage: Here’s the tension: giving can become performative. The person who gives for recognition is not giving. They are purchasing reputation. The person who gives quietly, without fanfare, without naming rights, without expectation of return — that is giving. Mr. Patel's name will not be on the community centre. The scholarships do not bear his name. He gives because it is right — not because it looks good. The most powerful giving is invisible.

entries.proposedWording: Retain reflection on motives while acknowledging different legitimate forms of giving and recognition. Quiet need not mean secret from trusted support.

entries.exactPassage: Here’s the tension: the section you are avoiding is the section that will teach you the most. If you are avoiding the legacy section, it is because you do not want to confront your own mortality. If you are avoiding the values section, it is because you have not clarified what you stand for.
